policy.up_session: close_i > close_(i-1) strictly over the N transitions of the N+1 closes ending at the target; ties count in neither the up nor the down fraction
policy.drawdown: running peak and trough inside the N closes ending at the target inclusive; no all-time peak
policy.sma: exact sum/N of the same N closes, own computation with history.sma arithmetic (no result dependency)
policy.comparison: close/SMA - 1; close_above_sma is strict (equality is not above)

policy.population: every governed bar of the reset epoch from the first bar through the target, all READY (strict, no minimum beyond the target bar)
policy.direction: a positive-volume bar is up if close > open, down if close < open, flat otherwise (flat volume is in the denominators only); zero-volume bars contribute 0
policy.dollar_volume: actual_notional only, never close*volume; the total is the accepted session.bar.notional (no new output)

reference_fact_schemas.note: price_unit None REFERENCE roles are not compared by require_compatible_inputs; market roles (daily, bars) are. Rows inside one (instrument, session) group must be ordered by (effective_start_ns, reference_id) as the shared validator requires. The tape facts are the transport of operands whose identity belongs to contract G (EQ-158 #492); if G publishes a different carrier, a mapping amendment replaces the carrier only and the mathematics here is unchanged.

mathematics.value_basis: Closes, opens, highs, lows and leg prices are positive int64 coefficients at ConfigSpec.price_unit.scale; volumes and counts are int64; notional is a decimal128 coefficient at the same scale. All arithmetic is exact integer/rational; ratios and rates are rational, divided by 10^scale or by seconds only at publication, with one correctly rounded float64. Share-volume sums are checked int64 (OVERFLOW if a published int64 sum exceeds 2^63-1); total volume, total notional and window sums used only as denominators are exact wide integers.
mathematics.session_projection: closes C_i on the daily governed grid, target t, window N. up_session_fraction = #{i in t-N+1..t : C_i > C_(i-1)} / N; down_session_fraction = #{C_i < C_(i-1)} / N; both need the N+1 closes t-N..t. Over the N closes w = C_(t-N+1)..C_t: M = max w, m = min w, S = sum w. drawdown_fraction = (M - C_t)/M; max_drawdown_fraction = max over i of (R_i - C_i)/R_i with R_i the running maximum of w up to i; distance_from_low_fraction = (C_t - m)/m; close_vs_sma_fraction = C_t/(S/N) - 1 = N*C_t/S - 1; close_above_sma = (N*C_t > S). Every denominator is positive (prices are positive), so zero_denominator is unreachable for this producer. Fractions of N are exact; max drawdown is the largest peak-to-trough decline inside the window, which differs from the current drawdown (SP05).
mathematics.bar_projection: bars i = 0..t of the reset epoch, volume V_i, actual notional N_i (0 for a proven-empty bar). up bar: V_i > 0 and C_i > O_i; down bar: V_i > 0 and C_i < O_i. up_volume = sum V_i over up bars, down_volume likewise (int64 shares); up_volume_fraction = up_volume / sum of all V_i; up_dollar_volume = sum N_i over up bars (decimal128 coefficient, currency = coefficient/10^scale); down_dollar_volume likewise; up_dollar_volume_fraction = up_dollar_volume / sum of all N_i. Zero total volume (or zero total notional) makes the fraction not_applicable/zero_denominator while the sums are available zeros. A flat bar contributes to neither side, only to the totals. The epoch total of notional is session.bar.notional and is not duplicated.
mathematics.relative_excess: leg witnesses: start price S, end price E with times; return r = E/S - 1. excess(role, profile) = r_instrument - r_benchmark exactly, using the profile's start facts and the shared end fact. Eligibility (all required, otherwise the reasons below): (1) both legs' start and end facts and, for sector, the membership fact are present, known (known_at <= K) and non-null; (2) end time <= cutoff C, otherwise future_market; (3) |end_instrument - end_benchmark| <= alignment_tolerance_ns; (4) cutoff - end <= max_endpoint_age_ns for each end; (5) per leg, start act == end act (action snapshot); (6) profile prior_close: the start fact's session differs from the end fact's session and is the same session for instrument and benchmark; profile window_start: start and end share one session for both legs, |(end - start) - window_ns| <= alignment_tolerance_ns for each leg and |start_instrument - start_benchmark| <= alignment_tolerance_ns; (7) sector: the membership fact binds the instrument to the configured sector_benchmark_id and is effective at or before the instrument end time. Failures of (3)-(7) are ineligible; an end after the cutoff is future_market. core outputs: for the declared core benchmarks b_1..b_K (K 2..16) the returns r_k with the same eligibility per benchmark leg; a benchmark that is not eligible makes the population partial (partial_universe, values withheld); among eligible benchmarks the end times (and for window_start the start times) must agree within the tolerance and share sessions, else ineligible. direction_agreement_fraction = max(#up, #down, #zero)/K with up r>0, down r<0, zero r=0 (zero is a class, ties between classes give the same maximum); return_dispersion_fraction = max r_k - min r_k (range, exact).
mathematics.rate_projection: tape outputs: a window [s,e) with e - s = window_ns exactly, e <= C and C - e <= max_endpoint_age_ns. trade_rate = count / (window_ns/1e9) trades per second; share_volume_rate = volume / (window_ns/1e9) shares per second; notional_rate = (notional/10^scale) / (window_ns/1e9) currency per second. raw_return_fraction = E/S - 1 from the window_start slot A witnesses: both facts READY, same session, act equal, |(end-start) - window_ns| <= alignment_tolerance_ns, end <= C, C - end <= max_endpoint_age_ns. return_rate_difference = (r_A - r_B) / (window_ns/1e9): rate_A = r_A/(window_ns/1e9), rate_B likewise for two windows of the same declared duration; the age bound applies to window A only; adjacency adjacent requires |start_A - end_B| <= alignment_tolerance_ns, disjoint requires end_B - start_A <= alignment_tolerance_ns (B entirely before A). Window A's end is the later one.
mathematics.publication: exact rational then one correctly rounded float64; bool and int64 and decimal128 exact; decimal128 outputs publish the integer coefficient at the PriceUnit scale

acceptance_rules.exact_float64: reference is a dyadic rational with numerator below 2^53 reached by exact integer/rational arithmetic, so any exact-rational or Decimal120 path produces it without rounding; the published float64 must equal the hex bit for bit
acceptance_rules.exact_plus_zero: reference exactly 0 from exact arithmetic (equal integers subtract to zero, an exact count of zero, ln of an exact ratio 1): bit-exact +0.0, never -0.0
acceptance_rules.tolerance: abs(y - r) <= max(8*ulp(r), 1e-12*abs(r)) with r the fixture float64 (the R17 numeric error contract, docs/api/INTRADAY.md, Numeric error contract and capabilities); also used for every value whose computation passes through a logarithm, even when the reference is dyadic, so implementations need not special-case it
acceptance_rules.exact_integer: int64 and decimal128 outputs are exact (decimal128 as the integer coefficient at the PriceUnit scale)

fixture_notation: compact, NOT canonical wire. K = 100 knowledge cutoff, default known_at 50. Session projection (SP): `closes` lists the governed daily closes 0..t, the target is the last unless `target` names an earlier index; an integer is a close, 'absent', 'gap', 'null' as in the sibling contract, {row, ka} an explicit known_at. Bar projection (BP): `bars` lists epoch bars [O,H,L,C,V,N] (N the actual notional or null), 'empty' a proven-empty zero-volume bar (READY with 0, unlike the path contract), 'absent', 'gap', 'null' a null-volume row, {row, ka}; notional_column=false means the actual_notional column is not delivered. Relative excess (RX/CB): C is the cutoff; times are small integer nanoseconds; `facts` are leg facts {inst, kind start|end, t witness time, p price coefficient, ss session id, pf profile (start only), act action snapshot, rev revision, ka known_at}; `membership` facts {inst, bound benchmark id, eff effective-from, ka}; instrument is the target X; the benchmark ids are in params. Rate projection (RP): times are integer nanoseconds (written as seconds times 10^9); `tape` facts {kind count|volume|notional, s, e, v canonical integer, ka}; `legs` facts {inst, kind, slot A|B, t, p, ss, act, rev, ka}. `unit.scale` is the price scale; `outputs` lists the selected feature ids and a fixture evaluates every listed output. Float results carry the exact rational, the float64, float.hex and the acceptance rule; int64 and decimal128 results carry the exact integer (decimal128 with its scale). Refusal fixtures are mutations of a named result fixture: `mutation` is the list of set/delete operations on `fixture.*` (the base fixture) and `ctx.*` (config unit, batch unit and adjustment, features, capability); a slot or row marker {mk: ...} stands for a canonical-wire defect named in the description.

decisions_proposed.decision: EQ-172 is one story with four producers. Scope map: up-session fractions -> session_projection up/down fractions; core-benchmark agreement/dispersion -> relative_excess core outputs; scalar SMA comparison -> close_vs_sma_fraction and close_above_sma; relative momentum comparison -> no new output (completed-history spreads are the accepted relative.market_return/relative.sector_return, current-endpoint and rolling spreads are the six excess outputs); dollar-volume/up-volume -> bar_projection; drawdown/distance -> session_projection; trailing trade/notional rates -> rate_projection; October 21 clarification -> six excess outputs; proposed raw return/share-volume rate/rate difference -> rate_projection. EQ-161 path efficiency is the sibling file.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: one monolithic producer; one file per producer
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Strict inequality on adjacent governed closes over N transitions (N+1 closes ending at the target); a tie is neither up nor down, so up + down <= 1; separate up and down fractions are published. The denominator is N, the number of transitions, never the observed count (a hole blocks).
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: ties count as up; ties excluded from the denominator; one signed score
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Closes only, window of N closes ending at the target inclusive; peak and trough are found inside the window (no all-time or anchored peak, so the output is a finite window with finite recovery). Three outputs: current drawdown from the window peak, maximum drawdown inside the window (running peak), distance of the close above the window low. All are non-negative fractions.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: all-time or session high; high/low rather than close; log drawdown
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: close_vs_sma_fraction = close/SMA - 1 with the SMA computed exactly (sum/N) from the same N closes. It uses the arithmetic of the accepted history.sma but is its own computation (no result edge), following the OQ-3 precedent of the EF3 mean companion: reuse of a published SMA result is unproved against the exact closure, and a result edge would couple readiness. close_above_sma is strict; equality is false (CONTEXT_FORMULAS: equality is not above), and a consumer wanting a tolerance supplies it in a policy layer, not here.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: consume history.sma as an operand; tolerance band
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: No new output. A momentum comparison of instrument versus benchmark over a completed governed horizon is exactly relative.market_return / relative.sector_return (r_symbol - r_benchmark), reusable when grid, horizon and endpoint mode are identical; the current-endpoint and rolling-interval spreads are the six excess outputs and must not be relabelled as completed-history values. Worked equivalence: 100->110 and 200->210 give 1/20 in both (RX01 equals the CONTEXT_FORMULAS example). Beta/residual stay with EQ-153.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: a new momentum-gap output; relabelling the existing outputs
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: A positive-volume bar is up if close > open and down if close < open (intra-bar direction). The first bar is included, nothing depends on a predecessor close or an overnight change, and the rule differs from OBV (which compares closes). Flat bars are in the denominators only. Zero-volume bars have null OHLC, contribute 0 and are READY observations (unlike the path contract, where a price is required).
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: tick rule on successive closes; typical-price direction; classify the first bar from the previous session close
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Dollar volume is actual traded notional only (EF1 rule: no close*volume or typical-price proxy). A positive-volume bar must supply actual_notional for a dollar output to be ready; a missing amount still leaves the volume outputs ready (BP06) and an absent column makes only the dollar outputs absent_input (BP07). Total epoch notional is the accepted session.bar.notional; this contract adds only the up/down split and its fraction (explicit no-change reuse decision).
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: close*volume proxy; a total dollar-volume output
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: bar_projection covers every bar from the first bar through the target bar, strictly: any unready bar blocks all outputs that need its fields. There is no window parameter and no minimum; a one-bar epoch is valid (BP14). Trailing windows over trades are rate_projection's, not this producer's.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: trailing N bars; min coverage
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Excess = r_instrument - r_benchmark, the arithmetic spread of simple returns formed by the library from exact start and end price witnesses, published as a fraction (0.05, not 5, not a ratio (1+r)/(1+b)-1). The library never accepts a pre-rounded float return. The subtraction and the fraction presentation are frozen separately from any percent presentation, which is a consumer matter.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: ratio of gross returns; log excess; percentage points
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: ef4.leg.start carries a profile label (prior_close, window_start, regular_open); the prior-close and rolling-window outputs consume different start facts and one shared end fact per instrument. A prior-close return and a regular-open return are different profiles: regular_open is accepted as a label for later consumers but no I2 output consumes it, and a leg that has only a regular_open start gives absent_input for the prior-close output (RX15). A prior_close start must belong to a session different from the endpoint's (RX14).
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: one start fact per leg with a flag; unlabeled start prices
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: alignment_tolerance_ns and max_endpoint_age_ns are explicit parameters with no default. Misalignment, a window duration that differs from window_ns by more than the tolerance, staleness beyond the age, a wrong session or phase, an action snapshot mismatch or a membership mismatch are ineligible (missing_input). An endpoint after the query cutoff is future_market (incomplete_coverage); the library never selects an earlier known row to hide a required future or unknown endpoint, and an unknown or later-known fact is unknown_availability or future_knowledge. An endpoint exactly at the cutoff is allowed.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: default tolerance; nearest-time matching; fall back to the last known row
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: The sector benchmark is bound by config id and by an explicit causal membership fact whose text names the benchmark instrument; it is never inferred from a sector string (RX24). Membership must be known, effective at or before the instrument endpoint and bound to the configured id. A missing sector membership blocks only the sector outputs (RX07); primary and secondary outputs stay ready. Each role must bind its own instrument and none may equal the target (self-benchmark refusal).
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: infer the benchmark from a sector label; one barrier for all roles
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Each leg's start and end must carry the same per-instrument action snapshot id (otherwise ineligible, RX16, RP18); snapshots of different instruments need not match because they are retained independently. The record revision is retained as evidence and not compared. Currency and adjustment policy are the ConfigSpec price unit and adjustment (INVALID_UNIT and UNSUPPORTED_ADJUSTMENT otherwise).
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: require equal snapshots across instruments; compare revisions
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Over K = 2..16 declared core benchmarks with the same profile: direction agreement = (size of the largest class among up, down and zero)/K; return dispersion = max return - min return. The range is exact and needs no square root; K is small so a sample standard deviation is unstable and would not be exact. A partial population withholds both values (partial_universe, observed < expected), as the EF3 cohort rule; an unready member reports only partial_universe, not its own reason. Mutual alignment of members is required (ineligible).
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: population standard deviation; mean absolute deviation; fraction positive
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Rates divide the independently ready window aggregate by the declared duration window_ns (not by the span of events). The operand windows must equal window_ns exactly and end at or before the cutoff and within max_endpoint_age_ns; zero is a valid observed value; an absent operand is absent_input. Operands are consumed by documented name only (tape count, tape volume, tape notional from contract G / EQ-158): this contract does not define trade windows, eligibility, signs, ties or notional ranking.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: elapsed time since the first event; a rolling count of events
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: raw_return_fraction is the simple return between the actual window start and end witnesses of the declared window; it is not the EF5 session return (open to endpoint) nor the EF1 open-to-endpoint return. return_rate_difference compares two equal-duration windows A (later) and B (earlier): (r_A - r_B)/(window_ns seconds), i.e. rate_A - rate_B; adjacency adjacent or disjoint is a parameter. The age bound applies to A only. The value has the dimension of a rate (fraction_per_second); dividing by the time between windows would be an acceleration, which stays with EQ-171.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: rates over different durations; implicit adjacency; acceleration
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: A window never spans sessions: start and end witnesses of a rolling window share one session (RP17); bar_projection uses the reset epoch; daily projections are on the governed daily grid; carry is not supported.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: carry across the open
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: The precedence of the merged EF3 robust-pace contract is reused unchanged. Compatibility failures are ineligible (missing_input), future endpoints future_market, unready core members partial_universe. Counts per output are in the quality block; an available output has observed = expected.

decisions_proposed.decision: fraction, shares, shares/s, currency (decimal128 coefficient at the PriceUnit scale) and boolean exist. New strings: trades_per_second, currency_per_second and fraction_per_second (planned spelling of EQ-171). A trade rate could reuse 1/s, but a count per second is not a rate of a dimensionless quantity in the same sense as adaptive.volume.peak_relative_acceleration, so a distinct string avoids ambiguity.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: reuse 1/s; invent no units and publish unitless
decisions_proposed.state: coordinator-decided (accepted as proposed), pending owner review

decisions_proposed.decision: Exact integer/rational arithmetic with one correctly rounded float64; no logarithm or square root occurs in this contract, so every fixture output is exact_float64, exact_plus_zero or tolerance (non-dyadic rationals) plus exact_integer and exact_bool. No Decimal path is required. Sums of share volumes are checked int64 (OVERFLOW); denominators use wide exact integers.
decisions_proposed.alternatives: alternatives: float accumulation

decisions_proposed.decision: EQ-158 #492 (contract G) supplies tape count, volume and notional by those documented names only; contract H (quote/VWAP) supplies nothing here and is not referenced. EQ-166/EQ-167 supply the prior close and endpoint price primitives that the I/O layer maps into the leg facts (the library only reads the facts), EQ-168 supplies the causal sector membership, EQ-153 stays the beta/residual owner. The EQ-155 edge is retained as an allocated prerequisite but no I2 output consumes an EQ-155 result (OQ-J3).

open_questions.text: RULING: use the spelling planned by EQ-171 (fraction_per_second) so the two stories register one string.
RULING: the three ef4.tape.* fact kinds are a provisional carrier because contract G has not merged; if G defines its own carrier the I/O mapping changes and the mathematics does not.

RULING (conservative): no I2 output consumes a robust-history result in v1; the EQ-155 dependency is kept as allocated and any rank or median of a projection over history is composed by ef3.robust_history with a supplied series. The owner may drop or re-route the edge.
RULING: unchanged owners (EQ-153) and existing outputs; no new momentum-gap output.
RULING: all comparison outputs are fractions; a percent display is a consumer or sink presentation.
RULING: packages/features EF4 module, config namespace ef4.*, separate catalog; no package version bump.
RULING: closes only in v1; a high/low drawdown is a later policy label.

layer_responsibilities.library: admission of the supplied rows, facts and context, closure and eligibility per output, exact sums, returns, ratios and rates, quality, evidence and every library refusal; pure and deterministic with exact rational intermediates and one final rounding; one shared closure preparation per producer reused across its outputs without coupling their readiness
layer_responsibilities.io_613: maps ordered closes and bars, leg witnesses with original known_at and revision, memberships and the tape-window operands exactly as supplied (including the explicit start/reference identity, endpoint identity and time, requested interval and phase, cutoff, revision and per-instrument action snapshot); maps results (int64, decimal128, bool, hex-exact float64, status, reasons, counts, witnesses) to the sink conversion; never derives a return, chooses a benchmark or window, infers a benchmark from a sector string, fills, bridges or replaces an unknown endpoint with an earlier known row, converts scale or currency, or computes a rate
layer_responsibilities.worker_614: routes each selected output to its own operands only (a sector gap never blocks a market comparison; a missing count never blocks a volume rate), shares bounded closures and facts, keeps independent readiness, executes one config per complete result, binds inputs and the config digest and persists the library result unchanged; direct, adapter, worker and stored results must be identical, including refusal class

non_goals: no acquisition of prices, volumes, trades, benchmarks, memberships, calendars or schedules; no clock or I/O
no default window, minimum history, tolerance, age, adjacency, normalization or threshold; every convention parameter is explicit and part of the config identity and digest
no scanner, alert, episode, rank-over-history or catalogue policy (EF8 #518-#520 own policy)
no update, restore or merge; batch and full replay only
no new DataKind, DTO, codec, scheduler, validator or error code; no change to any shared validator
no performance, parity, release or publication claim; no private-source equivalence or source formula
no relative momentum output: completed-history momentum spreads are relative.market_return and relative.sector_return (no change); beta, correlation and residual outputs stay with EQ-153
no breadth or cohort construction: ef3.session_breadth (EQ-220) and ef3.observed_breadth keep their outputs; up_volume here is a single-instrument epoch projection, not breadth up_volume
no quote, spread or VWAP operand (contract H) and no redefinition of trade windows, signs or notional top-K (contract G)
no technical return/velocity/acceleration (EQ-171 #512, EF5): the rate difference here is a difference of two window rates, never a second time derivative
no percentile or rank of any projection over history or cohort; no EQ-155 result is consumed in v1 (see OQ-J3)
coordinator_freeze: Frozen as ef4-proj1, ef4-rel1 and ef4-rate1 (v1) for implementation once this PR merges (coordinator statement; no review or acceptance claim by the author). Any change to a convention, label semantics, header, role, fact schema or fixture after merge requires a new policy label and an amendment document. No defaults for windows, tolerances, ages, adjacency or benchmark ids.
hosting: packages/features EF4 module, config namespace ef4.*, separate catalog; describe_intraday() and its digest unchanged; no package version bump
header_ledger_to_be_applied: the 26 headers above are to be applied by a sibling amendment document after the freeze; units fraction, shares, shares/s, currency, boolean already exist; three unit strings are new to the ledger: trades_per_second, currency_per_second and fraction_per_second (the last is the spelling already planned by EQ-171 #512 in the 47-output manifest; whichever amendment merges first registers it)
